question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

To harm oneself in a futile attempt to hurt or spite another person.
option_1: Cut off your nose to spite your face
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Cut off your nose to spite your face.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "Cut off your nose to spite your face" means to take a self-destructive action out of anger or resentment, so that you end up hurting yourself more than the person you are angry with (क्रोध में आत्मघाती कदम उठाना).
◦ Example: Refusing a well-deserved promotion just to annoy your boss is cutting off your nose to spite your face.

 

• The phrase warns against letting anger override reason; the "revenge" backfires on the doer, which exactly matches the given meaning – harming oneself in a futile attempt to spite another.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Bite the bullet (कठिनाई का साहसपूर्वक सामना करना): to endure a painful or unavoidable situation bravely.

 

• Option 3: Burn one's bridges (वापसी के रास्ते बंद करना): to act so as to make return or reconciliation impossible.

 

• Option 4: Throw in the towel (हार मान लेना): to admit defeat and give up (an idiom drawn from boxing).

 

NOTE

 

• SSC frequently tests self-harm/anger idioms; distinguish them by the intent behind the action. Related: "add fuel to the fire", "dig your own grave", "shoot yourself in the foot" (all self-inflicted harm).

question: Choose the correctly spelt word from the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Liaison.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is "Liaison" – a communication or working relationship between groups or people (सम्पर्क/तालमेल). Note the sequence li-ai-son: an "ai" followed by "so".
◦ Example: She acts as the liaison between the school and the parents.

 

• It derives from the French verb "lier" (to bind); a person maintaining contact between parties is a "liaison officer". Mnemonic: liAIson has "AI" in the middle, like an aid binding two sides.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Liason": wrong – the second "i" is dropped.

 

• Option 2 "Liasion": wrong – the vowels "ai" are reversed to "asi".

 

• Option 4 "Liaision": wrong – an extra "i" is inserted.

 

NOTE

 

• Related tricky spellings often tested by SSC: maintenance, reconnaissance, questionnaire, millennium, harass.

question: Which of the following words is correctly spelt?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Bureaucracy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is "Bureaucracy" – a system of government or administration run by officials (नौकरशाही). It is built from "bureau" + "-cracy", so keep the exact sequence B-U-R-E-A-U-C-R-A-C-Y.

 

• Root: French "bureau" (desk/office) + Greek "-cracy" (rule). Family words: bureaucrat, bureaucratic.
◦ Example: Excessive bureaucracy delayed the approval of the project.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Bureacracy": wrong – the "u" after "burea" is missing.

 

• Option 2 "Bureaucrasy": wrong – "c" is replaced by "s" (-crasy).

 

• Option 3 "Beaurocracy": wrong – the "ea" is reversed and "u" misplaced.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-cracy" words for revision: democracy, aristocracy, meritocracy, autocracy, plutocracy.

question:
Choose the correct synonym for the underlined word.

The abandoned mansion had fallen into a decrepit state over the decades.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Dilapidated.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The word "Decrepit" means worn out or ruined because of age or long neglect (जर्जर/जीर्ण-शीर्ण). Its closest synonym here is "Dilapidated", meaning in a state of disrepair.
◦ Example: The decrepit/dilapidated building was declared unsafe.

 

• "Decrepit" can also describe people weakened by old age; other synonyms are rickety, ramshackle, run-down, worn-out.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Pristine (बेदाग/नया जैसा): spotless, fresh and unspoiled – the opposite meaning.

 

• Option 3: Robust (मजबूत): strong and healthy – unrelated to decay.

 

• Option 4: Ornate (अलंकृत): heavily or elaborately decorated – unrelated.

 

NOTE

 

• Antonyms of decrepit: pristine, sturdy, sound, new. The word comes from Latin "decrepitus" (broken down with age).

question: Which of the following words is the closest synonym of the word “ephemeral”?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Transient.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The word "Ephemeral" means lasting for a very short time (क्षणभंगुर). Its closest synonym is "Transient" (fleeting, momentary).
◦ Example: The beauty of a rainbow is ephemeral/transient.

 

• "Ephemeral" comes from Greek "ephemeros" (lasting only a day); other synonyms are fleeting, transitory, momentary, short-lived.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Eternal (शाश्वत): everlasting, permanent – the exact opposite.

 

• Option 3: Tangible (मूर्त/स्पर्श योग्य): able to be touched or perceived physically – unrelated.

 

• Option 4: Robust (मजबूत): strong and vigorous – unrelated.

 

NOTE

 

• Antonyms of ephemeral: permanent, enduring, eternal, perpetual, everlasting.

question:
There are four underlined words in the sentence given below. One of them is misspelt. Choose the option with the misspelt word.

The entrepreneur's perseverance ensured the swift accomodation of every grievance raised by the staff.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. accomodation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is "accommodation", which takes a double "c" and a double "m" (आवास/समायोजन). The given form "accomodation" has only a single "m", so it is misspelt.
◦ Memory hook: accommodation can hold two cots (cc) and two mattresses (mm).

 

• The other three underlined words are all spelt correctly, so they are not the answer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "entrepreneur" (उद्यमी): correct – note the French ending -eur.

 

• Option 2 "perseverance" (दृढ़ता/लगन): correct – per-se-ver-ance, no double letters.

 

• Option 3 "grievance" (शिकायत): correct – griev + ance (from "grieve").

 

NOTE

 

• Frequently confused double-letter spellings in SSC: accommodation, occurrence, embarrass, millennium, committee.

question: Choose the misspelt word from the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Harrassment.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is "Harassment" with a single "r" and a double "s" (उत्पीड़न). The given "Harrassment" wrongly doubles the "r", so it is the misspelt word.
◦ Memory hook: it is har-ASS-ment – one r, two s.

 

• The remaining three options are all correctly spelt, so they cannot be the answer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "Sacrilegious" (धर्मनिंदक): correct – note it is spelt sacri-leg-ious (not like "religious").

 

• Option 3 "Liquefy" (द्रवित करना): correct – uses "e" before -fy (like putrefy, stupefy, rarefy).

 

• Option 4 "Inoculate" (टीका लगाना): correct – single "n" and single "c".

 

NOTE

 

• Watch the r/s pattern in similar words: embarrassment (rr, ss), harassment (r, ss), professor (one f, two s wrong – actually ss). Revise: occurrence, recommend, necessary.

question: Choose the word that is most opposite in meaning to “benevolent”.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Malevolent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The word "Benevolent" means kind and wishing to do good (दयालु/परोपकारी). Its antonym is "Malevolent", meaning wishing harm or evil to others (द्वेषपूर्ण).
◦ Prefix clue: "bene-" = good, "male-" = bad/evil.

 

• Word family: benefactor, beneficial, benefit (good) vs malice, malicious, malefactor (bad). Example: The malevolent glare warned them of trouble.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Generous (उदार): giving freely – a synonym of benevolent, not an antonym.

 

• Option 2: Cordial (सौहार्दपूर्ण): warm and friendly – a synonym, not opposite.

 

• Option 4: Amiable (मिलनसार): good-natured and likeable – a synonym, not opposite.

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of benevolent: kind-hearted, charitable, magnanimous, humane. Remember the "bene-" (good) vs "male-" (evil) prefix pair for antonym questions.

question: Choose the word that is the antonym of “candid”.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Evasive.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The word "Candid" means truthful, open and straightforward (स्पष्टवादी/निष्कपट). Its antonym is "Evasive", meaning avoiding a direct answer (टालमटोल करने वाला).
◦ Example: He gave an evasive reply instead of a candid one.

 

• "Evasive" is related to "evade" (to escape or dodge); a memory hook is the phrase "Candid Camera", which captures unguarded, genuine moments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Frank (स्पष्ट): honest and direct – a synonym of candid.

 

• Option 3: Blunt (बेबाक): direct to the point of rudeness – a synonym of candid.

 

• Option 4: Sincere (निष्कपट): honest and genuine – a synonym of candid.

 

NOTE

 

• Other antonyms of candid: guarded, secretive, indirect, cagey, cryptic. Synonyms: forthright, open, honest, direct.

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A supposed remedy that cures all diseases or solves all problems.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Panacea.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A "Panacea" is a universal remedy that supposedly cures all diseases or solves all difficulties (रामबाण/सर्वरोगनाशक).
◦ Example: There is no single panacea for the country's economic problems.

 

• The word comes from Panakeia, the Greek goddess of universal remedy; it is often used figuratively for an over-simple solution to a complex problem.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Placebo (छद्म/मिथ्या औषधि): a harmless dummy treatment given for psychological effect (Latin "I shall please"); used in medical trials.

 

• Option 2: Antidote (मारक/प्रतिविष): a specific remedy that counters a particular poison, not all diseases.

 

• Option 3: Elixir (अमृत/संजीवनी): a magical potion said to prolong life or turn metal to gold.

 

NOTE

 

• Related one-word substitutions: remedy (specific cure), palliative (relieves without curing), cure-all (= panacea).

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An abnormal or extreme fear of heights.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Acrophobia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Acrophobia" is the extreme or irrational fear of heights (ऊँचाई का भय). The root "acro-" means height/topmost (as in acropolis, acrobat).
◦ Example: Her acrophobia made the glass skywalk terrifying.

 

• The suffix "-phobia" (fear) is common in one-word substitutions, so identifying the root (acro- = height) fixes the answer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Agoraphobia (खुले/सार्वजनिक स्थान का भय): fear of open or public spaces (Greek "agora" = marketplace).

 

• Option 3: Claustrophobia (बंद स्थान का भय): fear of enclosed spaces (Latin "claustrum" = enclosed).

 

• Option 4: Hydrophobia (जल का भय): fear of water; also a symptom of rabies.

 

NOTE

 

• Other common SSC phobias: Xenophobia (foreigners), Nyctophobia (darkness), Pyrophobia (fire), Arachnophobia (spiders).

question:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

The new professor is well versed ________ classical music and comparative literature.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. in.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The fixed expression is "versed in", meaning skilled or knowledgeable in a subject (प्रवीण/निपुण). Hence the blank takes "in": "well versed in classical music."
◦ Example: She is well versed in constitutional law.

 

• Adjectives of proficiency generally pair with "in": proficient in, expert in, skilled in. Compare: we say "good at" a skill but "versed in" a subject/field.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "with": wrong – "versed with" is not standard usage.

 

• Option 2 "at": wrong – "at" suits skills (good at chess), not this collocation.

 

• Option 4 "on": wrong – not used with "versed".

 

NOTE

 

• Revise fixed "in" collocations: absorbed in, engrossed in, deficient in, interested in, well versed in.

question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?

The committee rejected his proposal.
option_1: His proposal was rejected by the committee.
option_2: His proposal is rejected by the committee.
option_3: His proposal were rejected by the committee.
option_4: His proposal has been rejected by the committee.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. His proposal was rejected by the committee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The active sentence is in the simple past with a singular object ("his proposal"). The passive rule for simple past is object + was/were + past participle (V3) + by + subject.
◦ So: His proposal (singular) + was + rejected + by the committee.

 

• The tense must be preserved while changing voice, and the singular subject "proposal" takes "was", not "were".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (is rejected): wrong – uses present tense "is" instead of the past.

 

• Option 3 (were rejected): wrong – uses plural "were" for a singular subject.

 

• Option 4 (has been rejected): wrong – changes the tense to present perfect.

 

NOTE

 

• Voice rule summary: Simple Past passive = was/were + V3; the object becomes the subject and the agent is introduced with "by".

question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?

Will they announce the results tomorrow?
option_1: Will the results announced by them tomorrow?
option_2: Will be the results announced by them tomorrow?
option_3: Will the results being announced by them tomorrow?
option_4: Will the results be announced by them tomorrow?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Will the results be announced by them tomorrow?

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• For a future interrogative sentence, the passive structure is Will + object + be + past participle (V3) + by + subject.
◦ So: Will + the results + be + announced + by them + tomorrow?

 

• The auxiliary "Will" stays at the front in a question, and "be" is essential before the past participle in the future passive.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: wrong – omits "be" (Will the results announced...).

 

• Option 2: wrong – misplaces "be" before the subject (Will be the results...).

 

• Option 3: wrongly uses "being" instead of "be".

 

NOTE

 

• Future passive rule: will + be + V3. In interrogatives the modal leads; the agent "by them" follows the participle.

question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?

Let the poem be recited by the children.
option_2: Let the children recite the poem.
option_3: The children will recite the poem.
option_4: Let the poem recite the children.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Let the children recite the poem.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An imperative passive of the form "Let + object + be + V3 (+ by + agent)" converts to active as "Let + agent + base verb + object".
◦ So: "Let the poem be recited by the children" → "Let the children recite the poem."

 

• The imperative/permissive tone carried by "Let" must be retained; the sentence should not become a plain statement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (The children recited the poem.): wrong – becomes a past-tense statement, losing the imperative "Let".

 

• Option 3 (The children will recite the poem.): wrong – adds a future tense not in the original.

 

• Option 4 (Let the poem recite the children.): wrong – reverses subject and object, making it meaningless.

 

NOTE

 

• Example pattern: "Let the door be closed" → "Let him close the door." Keep the base form of the verb after the agent.

question:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

In terms of experience, the senior surgeon is far superior ________ all her colleagues.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. to.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Latin-derived comparatives such as superior, inferior, senior, junior, prior, anterior, posterior are always followed by "to", never "than".
◦ So: "far superior to all her colleagues."

 

• The same "to" pattern applies to "prefer X to Y". Saying "superior than" is a classic error.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "than": wrong – "than" follows ordinary comparatives (taller than), not "superior".

 

• Option 2 "from": wrong – "different from", but not "superior from".

 

• Option 4 "over": wrong – not the standard preposition with "superior".

 

NOTE

 

• Remember the group taking "to": superior/inferior/senior/junior/prior/anterior/posterior + to. Example: This model is inferior to the earlier one.

question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option which can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: “No Improvement Required.”

Hardly had she finished her closing speech when the audience erupts into thunderous applause.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. erupted into thunderous applause.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correlative structure "Hardly had + subject + past participle ... when ..." requires the second clause to be in the simple past. Since the first clause uses the past perfect ("had finished"), the present-tense "erupts" is wrong and must become "erupted".
◦ Correct: "Hardly had she finished her closing speech when the audience erupted into thunderous applause."

 

• Note the inversion: after "Hardly" the auxiliary "had" comes before the subject.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (had erupted): wrong – the "when" clause should be simple past, not another past perfect.

 

• Option 3 (erupt): wrong – bare present form does not agree with the past-perfect first clause.

 

• Option 4 (No improvement required): wrong – the present tense "erupts" is clearly ungrammatical here.

 

NOTE

 

• Related correlatives: "Hardly/Scarcely ... when ..." and "No sooner ... than ..." – both use past perfect + simple past with inversion. "Hardly" pairs with "when"; "No sooner" pairs with "than".

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. For weeks the old lighthouse keeper had noticed strange lights flickering far out on the water, but he had told no one.

A. Yet on that particular night the glow was brighter, and it drifted steadily towards the rocks below his tower.

B. He had always assumed they were the lamps of fishing boats returning late from the deeper channels.

C. Alarmed, he seized his logbook and began to record the hour, the wind, and the odd colour of the light.

D. As it drew nearer, he realised that no boat could move against so fierce a current without the roar of an engine.

S2. By dawn the light had vanished, and the keeper was left with a single page of frantic notes and no explanation at all.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. BADC.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The logical order is B-A-D-C. After S1 introduces the mysterious lights, B gives the keeper's habitual assumption that they were fishing boats.
◦ B → A: "Yet ... that particular night" in A contrasts with the assumption in B, so B must precede A.

 

• A → D: "As it drew nearer" (D) follows the light that begins drifting closer in A. D → C: once he realises no boat could behave so (D), he is "Alarmed" and starts recording details (C), which leads into S2's "page of frantic notes".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (ADBC): wrong – places A before B, but A's "Yet" needs the assumption in B first.

 

• Option 3 (DCBA): wrong – ends with A, leaving the recording (C) disconnected from S2's notes.

 

• Option 4 (BDAC): wrong – puts D before A, but "drew nearer" (D) needs the drifting light introduced in A.

 

NOTE

 

• Para-jumble tips: track link words (Yet, As, Alarmed) and pronoun/reference chains. Fix S1–S2 first, then order the middle by cause-and-effect.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. The invention of the mechanical clock in medieval Europe did far more than merely help people tell the time.

A. Before its arrival, the day had been measured loosely by the sun, the ringing of church bells, and the rhythm of daily labour.

B. The clock replaced this fluid sense of time with fixed, countable hours that were the same in summer and winter alike.

C. Gradually, punctuality came to be prized as a virtue, and lateness condemned as a fault that could be measured to the minute.

D. This new precision reshaped work, trade, and even prayer, binding whole communities to a single, rigid schedule.

S2. In this quiet way, one instrument helped lay the foundations of the disciplined, time-conscious modern world.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. ABDC.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The logical order is A-B-D-C. S1 claims the clock did more than tell time; A begins with "Before its arrival", so it naturally follows S1 by describing the older, loose way of measuring time.
◦ A → B: "this fluid sense of time" in B refers back to the loose measurement in A.

 

• B → D: "This new precision" in D points to the fixed hours introduced in B. D → C: C then draws the broad social conclusion (punctuality prized) that flows into S2's summary about the modern world.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (ADBC): wrong – D's "new precision" needs B's fixed hours first.

 

• Option 2 (BADC): wrong – B's "this fluid sense" needs A's loose measurement first.

 

• Option 3 (ABCD): wrong – ends with D, but C (the social conclusion) fits better just before S2.

 

NOTE

 

• Reference-tracking is the key skill: demonstrative phrases like "this fluid sense" and "this new precision" must point back to the immediately preceding idea.

question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: “No improvement required.”

The waiter served sandwiches to the children on paper plates.
option_1: to paper plates on the children
option_2: on the children to paper plates
option_3: on paper plates to the children
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. on paper plates to the children.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the original sentence the phrase "on paper plates" sits next to "the children", wrongly suggesting the children were on the plates – a misplaced modifier.
◦ Correct: "The waiter served sandwiches on paper plates to the children", placing "on paper plates" beside "sandwiches", which it actually describes.

 

• A modifier should sit as close as possible to the word it modifies to remove ambiguity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (to paper plates on the children): wrong – nonsensical; sandwiches are not served "to" plates.

 

• Option 2 (on the children to paper plates): wrong – still misplaces the phrases and is illogical.

 

• Option 4 (No improvement required): wrong – the original wording is ambiguous and needs correction.

 

NOTE

 

• Classic error type: misplaced/prepositional-phrase modifiers. Example fix: "She wore a hat on her head that was blue" → "She wore a blue hat on her head."

question:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:

Antibiotics were once hailed as the miracle that would banish infectious disease forever, yet the very success of these drugs now threatens to undo their promise. Every time an antibiotic is used, it kills the susceptible bacteria but spares the few that happen to carry resistance genes; these survivors multiply until, over generations, they come to dominate the population. The danger is accelerated by careless prescription, unfinished courses of treatment, and the vast quantities of antibiotics fed to livestock to promote growth rather than to cure illness. As resistance spreads, once-trivial infections threaten to become untreatable and routine surgeries grow perilous. What makes the crisis especially intractable is that bacteria reproduce with astonishing speed and can swap resistance genes across species, so that a defence evolved in one microbe may soon shield a wholly different one. Developing new antibiotics, meanwhile, is slow and rarely profitable, and few pharmaceutical firms pursue it. Scientists therefore argue that the wisest course is stewardship: using the drugs we still possess sparingly and precisely, so that these weapons are not blunted before any replacement can be found.

 

Which of the following best captures the central idea of the passage?
option_1: The overuse of antibiotics is eroding their effectiveness and calls for careful stewardship.
option_2: Antibiotics have permanently eliminated infectious disease across the world.
option_3: Pharmaceutical firms are competing fiercely to develop new antibiotics.
option_4: Livestock farming is the only cause of antibiotic resistance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. The overuse of antibiotics is eroding their effectiveness and calls for careful stewardship.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The passage argues that the very success and overuse of antibiotics breeds resistance, and it concludes that "the wisest course is stewardship" (समझदारी भरा प्रबंधन). Option 1 captures both the problem and the recommended response, which is exactly what a central idea should do.

 

• The concluding sentence of a passage frequently restates the main idea; here it advises using drugs "sparingly and precisely".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: wrong – contradicts the passage, which says the promise of eliminating disease is being undone.

 

• Option 3: wrong – opposite of "few pharmaceutical firms pursue it".

 

• Option 4: wrong – overstates one contributing factor (livestock) as the "only" cause.

 

NOTE

 

• For central-idea questions, beware extreme words like "only", "permanently", "never" in distractors; the best answer usually combines the main problem and the author's suggested response.

question:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:

Antibiotics were once hailed as the miracle that would banish infectious disease forever, yet the very success of these drugs now threatens to undo their promise. Every time an antibiotic is used, it kills the susceptible bacteria but spares the few that happen to carry resistance genes; these survivors multiply until, over generations, they come to dominate the population. The danger is accelerated by careless prescription, unfinished courses of treatment, and the vast quantities of antibiotics fed to livestock to promote growth rather than to cure illness. As resistance spreads, once-trivial infections threaten to become untreatable and routine surgeries grow perilous. What makes the crisis especially intractable is that bacteria reproduce with astonishing speed and can swap resistance genes across species, so that a defence evolved in one microbe may soon shield a wholly different one. Developing new antibiotics, meanwhile, is slow and rarely profitable, and few pharmaceutical firms pursue it. Scientists therefore argue that the wisest course is stewardship: using the drugs we still possess sparingly and precisely, so that these weapons are not blunted before any replacement can be found.

 

According to the passage, which of the following accelerates the spread of antibiotic resistance?
option_1: Prescribing antibiotics only when strictly necessary
option_2: Feeding large quantities of antibiotics to livestock to promote growth
option_3: Completing the full prescribed course of treatment
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Feeding large quantities of antibiotics to livestock to promote growth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The passage states that the danger is accelerated by "careless prescription, unfinished courses of treatment, and the vast quantities of antibiotics fed to livestock to promote growth". Option 2 matches this text directly.

 

• Detail questions require locating the exact supporting sentence; the three named accelerators are careless prescription, unfinished courses, and livestock use.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: wrong – prescribing only when necessary is a responsible practice, not an accelerator.

 

• Option 3: wrong – completing the full course is good practice; it is the *unfinished* course that accelerates resistance.

 

• Option 4: wrong – the passage says new antibiotics are rarely developed, and this does not accelerate resistance.

 

NOTE

 

• In detail questions, distractors often invert a stated cause into good practice. Read the whole clause to avoid partial matches.

As used in the passage, the word “intractable” most nearly means:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. difficult to manage or resolve.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Intractable" describes a problem that is hard to control or solve (दुर्दम्य/असाध्य). In context the crisis is called "especially intractable" because bacteria multiply fast and swap resistance genes, making the problem stubborn.

 

• Root clue: "tract-" (to handle/draw) + "in-" (not); compare "tractable" = manageable.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "easily solved": wrong – the exact opposite of the intended meaning.

 

• Option 2 "short-lived": wrong – relates to duration, not difficulty.

 

• Option 3 "mildly irritating": wrong – far too weak for a described "crisis".

 

NOTE

 

• Synonyms of intractable: unmanageable, obstinate, thorny, insoluble. In vocab-in-context items, use surrounding clues, not just the plain dictionary sense.

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions based on the passage:

Antibiotics were once hailed as the miracle that would banish infectious disease forever, yet the very success of these drugs now threatens to undo their promise. Every time an antibiotic is used, it kills the susceptible bacteria but spares the few that happen to carry resistance genes; these survivors multiply until, over generations, they come to dominate the population. The danger is accelerated by careless prescription, unfinished courses of treatment, and the vast quantities of antibiotics fed to livestock to promote growth rather than to cure illness. As resistance spreads, once-trivial infections threaten to become untreatable and routine surgeries grow perilous. What makes the crisis especially intractable is that bacteria reproduce with astonishing speed and can swap resistance genes across species, so that a defence evolved in one microbe may soon shield a wholly different one. Developing new antibiotics, meanwhile, is slow and rarely profitable, and few pharmaceutical firms pursue it. Scientists therefore argue that the wisest course is stewardship: using the drugs we still possess sparingly and precisely, so that these weapons are not blunted before any replacement can be found.

 

It can be inferred from the passage that pharmaceutical firms are reluctant to develop new antibiotics because:
option_1: the process is quick and highly profitable
option_2: bacteria cannot develop resistance to new drugs
option_3: the process is slow and yields little profit
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. the process is slow and yields little profit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The passage says developing new antibiotics "is slow and rarely profitable, and few pharmaceutical firms pursue it". The reasonable inference is that firms avoid it because it is slow and unprofitable.

 

• A valid inference is a logical, minimal step beyond the stated facts – grounded in the text, not in outside knowledge. The clue phrase is "slow and rarely profitable".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: wrong – directly contradicts the text (which says slow and rarely profitable).

 

• Option 2: wrong – the passage says bacteria readily develop and swap resistance.

 

• Option 4: wrong – no government ban is mentioned anywhere in the passage.

 

NOTE

 

• Reject inference options that introduce facts not mentioned in the text (e.g., government prohibition). Stay within what the passage supports.

Scientists therefore argue that the wisest course is stewardship: using the drugs we still possess sparingly and precisely, so that these weapons are not blunted before any replacement can be found.

 

The tone of the passage can best be described as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. concerned and cautionary.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The author highlights a growing danger ("threatens to undo their promise", "once-trivial infections threaten to become untreatable") and urges careful stewardship. This reflects a concerned and cautionary tone (चिंतित एवं सतर्कतापूर्ण).

 

• Tone is judged from the author's word choices and attitude; words like "danger", "perilous" and "crisis" signal concern, while the call for "stewardship" adds a cautionary, advisory note.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 "indifferent and dismissive": wrong – the author clearly cares and warns.

 

• Option 3 "joyful and celebratory": wrong – there is worry, not celebration.

 

• Option 4 "sarcastic and mocking": wrong – the passage is serious and earnest, not mocking.

 

NOTE

 

• Distinguish tone (author's attitude) from mere subject matter. Common SSC tone words: critical, optimistic, nostalgic, objective, cautionary.

question: The Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO) was established at Jamshedpur in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 1907.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO) was established in 1907 at Sakchi (later renamed Jamshedpur) in present-day Jharkhand. It was founded on the vision of Jamsetji Tata and formally set up by his son Dorabji Tata.

 

• It began producing steel in 1912 and was India's first large private-sector integrated steel plant. It is now known as Tata Steel.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• 1919: wrong – later than the actual founding year.

 

• 1911: wrong – close to first steel production (1912) but not the establishment year.

 

• 1875: wrong – predates the Tata steel venture entirely.

 

NOTE

 

• Jamshedpur lies on the banks of the Subarnarekha and Kharkai rivers. Later public-sector steel plants: Rourkela (1959, German help), Bhilai (USSR), Durgapur (UK).

question:
The Kakatiya dynasty, which flourished between the twelfth and fourteenth centuries, ruled over parts of which present-day areas?

I. Telangana
II. Andhra Pradesh
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Both I and II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kakatiyas ruled from their capital at Warangal (in present-day Telangana) and extended control over the coastal Andhra region, including the port of Motupalli (present-day Andhra Pradesh). Hence both statements I and II are correct.

 

• Rani Rudrama Devi was one of the few women to rule as a monarch in medieval India; Prataparudra II was the last powerful Kakatiya ruler.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Only I / Only II: wrong – the kingdom spanned both modern Telangana and coastal Andhra Pradesh.

 

• Neither I nor II: wrong – both regions were under Kakatiya rule.

 

NOTE

 

• Kakatiya monuments: the Thousand Pillar Temple and the Ramappa (Rudreshwara) Temple – a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2021). The kingdom fell to the forces of the Delhi Sultanate (Tughlaqs) in the 14th century.

question: Who among the following propounded the 'Dvaita' (dualism) school of Vedanta philosophy?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Madhvacharya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Madhvacharya (13th century) propounded the Dvaita (dualism) philosophy (द्वैतवाद), which holds that the individual soul (Jiva) and the Supreme (Brahman/Vishnu) are eternally distinct.

 

• It is a strongly Vaishnava tradition; these Vedanta schools differ mainly on the relation between Atman and Brahman.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ramanujacharya: founded Vishishtadvaita (qualified non-dualism).

 

• Nimbarkacharya: founded Dvaitadvaita (dualistic non-dualism).

 

• Vallabhacharya: founded Shuddhadvaita (pure non-dualism).

 

NOTE

 

• Adi Shankaracharya propounded Advaita (non-dualism). Memory chain: Shankara – Advaita, Ramanuja – Vishishtadvaita, Madhva – Dvaita.

question: Which of the following is the highest mountain peak lying entirely within the territory of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Nanda Devi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nanda Devi (7,816 m) in Uttarakhand is the highest peak lying entirely within Indian territory. It is the second highest peak in India overall.

 

• Kangchenjunga (8,586 m), though the highest peak of India, lies on the India–Nepal border, so it is not wholly within India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kangchenjunga: world's 3rd highest and India's highest peak, on the Sikkim–Nepal border – not entirely within India.

 

• Kamet (7,756 m): lower than Nanda Devi, in Uttarakhand near the Tibet border.

 

• Saltoro Kangri: lower, in the Karakoram (Siachen area).

 

NOTE

 

• The Nanda Devi Biosphere Reserve is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. K2 (Godwin-Austen) is India's highest point in the disputed Gilgit-Baltistan region.

question:
Consider the following statements about the later Vedic period:

I. Iron was known and referred to as 'krishna ayas' or 'shyama ayas'.
II. The people commonly used coined metallic money in trade.

 

Which of the statements is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Only I.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• During the later Vedic period, iron came into use and was called 'krishna ayas' or 'shyama ayas' (dark metal), so statement I is correct.

 

• Statement II is incorrect – coined metallic money did not exist then; the earliest punch-marked coins appeared only around the 6th century BCE, after the Vedic age. The later Vedic economy was largely agrarian and barter-based.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Only II / Both I and II: wrong – because coinage is anachronistic for the Vedic period.

 

• Neither I nor II: wrong – statement I about iron ('krishna/shyama ayas') is factually correct.

 

NOTE

 

• In the Rigveda, 'ayas' referred to copper or bronze; iron came later. The Painted Grey Ware (PGW) culture is linked to the later Vedic period; earliest coins = punch-marked (Janapada/Mahajanapada era).

question: At a chemical synapse, the nerve impulse is carried across the synaptic cleft from one neuron to the next mainly by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. neurotransmitters.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At a chemical synapse, the electrical impulse reaching the axon terminal triggers the release of chemical messengers called neurotransmitters (तंत्रिकाप्रेषी), which cross the synaptic cleft and bind to receptors on the next neuron, regenerating the impulse.

 

• Within a neuron, the impulse travels as an electrical (action) potential; only at the synapse is it carried chemically.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hormones: wrong – they travel through the blood, not across a synapse.

 

• Enzymes: wrong – they catalyse biochemical reactions, not impulse transfer.

 

• Electrolytes: wrong – ions like Na+/K+ generate the action potential but are not the cross-cleft messenger.

 

NOTE

 

• Common neurotransmitters: acetylcholine, dopamine, serotonin, GABA. The neuron–muscle junction is the neuromuscular junction. Flow direction: dendrite → cell body → axon → synapse.

question: The 'Sonepur Mela', regarded as one of Asia's largest cattle fairs, is held in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Sonepur Mela (also called Harihar Kshetra Mela) is held at Sonepur in Bihar, at the confluence of the Ganga and Gandak rivers, and is one of Asia's largest cattle fairs.

 

• It traditionally begins on Kartik Purnima and was historically famous for its large elephant trade.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Jharkhand / Odisha / West Bengal: wrong – the fair is specifically in Bihar (Saran district, near Hajipur).

 

• Other famous cattle fairs: Pushkar Fair (Rajasthan) and Nagaur Fair (Rajasthan).

 

NOTE

 

• Static-GK hook: link Sonepur → Bihar → Ganga+Gandak → Kartik Purnima. Pushkar (camel fair) and Nagaur (bullock fair) are the Rajasthan counterparts commonly asked.

question: In which year did Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Sikh Guru, attain martyrdom?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 1675.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Tegh Bahadur, the ninth Sikh Guru, was executed in Delhi in 1675 on the orders of the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb for defending religious freedom, notably that of the Kashmiri Pandits.

 

• He is remembered as 'Hind di Chadar' (the shield of India). Gurdwara Sis Ganj Sahib in Delhi marks the site of his martyrdom.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• 1666: wrong – that is the birth year of his successor, Guru Gobind Singh (the tenth Guru).

 

• 1699: wrong – the year the Khalsa was founded by Guru Gobind Singh.

 

• 1708: wrong – the year Guru Gobind Singh passed away.

 

NOTE

 

• Guru Tegh Bahadur composed hymns included in the Guru Granth Sahib. Key Sikh dates: Khalsa – 1699, Guru Gobind Singh born – 1666, died – 1708.

question: In terms of size, Mars is the ______ largest planet in the solar system.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. seventh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Arranged from largest to smallest, the planets are: Jupiter > Saturn > Uranus > Neptune > Earth > Venus > Mars > Mercury. Mars is therefore the seventh largest, with only Mercury being smaller.

 

• Mars is called the 'Red Planet' due to iron oxide (rust) on its surface.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• fifth: wrong – that rank belongs to Earth (largest of the terrestrial planets).

 

• sixth: wrong – that rank belongs to Venus.

 

• eighth: wrong – the eighth (smallest) is Mercury.

 

NOTE

 

• Largest planet = Jupiter; smallest = Mercury. Order by distance from Sun (different from size): Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.

question: What is the name of India's first indigenously developed anti-radiation missile, developed by the DRDO?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Rudram.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rudram (Rudram-1) is India's first indigenously developed anti-radiation missile, developed by the DRDO and tested in 2020. It is an air-to-surface missile designed to home in on and destroy enemy radar and communication sites.

 

• It gives the Indian Air Force SEAD (Suppression of Enemy Air Defence) capability and can be launched from Su-30 MKI aircraft.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nirbhay: long-range subsonic cruise missile.

 

• Astra: beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile.

 

• Prahaar: short-range surface-to-surface tactical missile.

 

NOTE

 

• DRDO missile family to revise: Agni & Prithvi (ballistic), BrahMos (supersonic cruise), Akash (SAM), Nag (anti-tank), Astra (air-to-air), Rudram (anti-radiation).

question: As per the Census of India 2011, which of the following states recorded the lowest population density?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Arunachal Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Census 2011, Arunachal Pradesh had the lowest population density among Indian states at about 17 persons per square kilometre, owing to its large hilly, forested area and small population.

 

• Bihar recorded the highest density among states (~1,106/km²).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sikkim / Mizoram: wrong – low but not the lowest among states.

 

• Andaman & Nicobar Islands: a Union Territory, not a state; the question specifically asks about states.

 

NOTE

 

• Census 2011 static hooks: National average density ≈ 382/km²; highest-density state = Bihar; among UTs, Delhi has the highest density.

question: India's first indigenously built aircraft carrier, INS Vikrant (commissioned in 2022), was constructed at which shipyard?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Cochin Shipyard Limited, Kochi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• INS Vikrant (IAC-1), India's first indigenously designed and built aircraft carrier, was constructed by Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL), Kochi and commissioned in September 2022.

 

• It placed India among a small group of nations able to build aircraft carriers; MiG-29K fighters operate from its deck.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mazagon Dock Limited, Mumbai: builds destroyers and submarines (e.g., Scorpene-class/Kalvari).

 

• Garden Reach Shipbuilders, Kolkata: builds frigates and corvettes.

 

• Hindustan Shipyard, Visakhapatnam: builds and repairs various naval/merchant vessels.

 

NOTE

 

• INS Vikrant is named after India's first aircraft carrier (retired 1997). India's other carrier is INS Vikramaditya (of Russian origin).

question: The indigenous mobile operating system 'BharOS', developed for enhanced privacy and security, was created by which institution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. IIT Madras.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• BharOS is an indigenous, privacy-focused mobile operating system developed by a firm incubated at IIT Madras (JandK Operations Pvt Ltd). It provides 'No Default Apps' (NDA) and access to trusted app stores.

 

• It is based on a version of the Android Open Source Project (AOSP) and aims to strengthen data sovereignty and security.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• IIT Delhi / IIT Bombay / IISc Bengaluru: wrong – BharOS is specifically an IIT Madras incubated project.

 

• It supports Native Over The Air (NOTA) updates and was publicly tested by Union ministers in January 2023.

 

NOTE

 

• It is aimed at organisations needing strict privacy and security. Link BharOS → IIT Madras → AOSP-based → 2023.

question: Under the FRBM (Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management) framework, the medium-term target is to bring the fiscal deficit down to ______ of GDP.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 3%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The FRBM Act framework set the medium-term target of reducing the Central government's fiscal deficit to 3% of GDP (राजकोषीय घाटा), along with eliminating the revenue deficit.

 

• The N.K. Singh Committee later reaffirmed the 3% fiscal deficit target and set a debt-to-GDP anchor of 40% for the Centre.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• 4% / 5% / 6%: wrong – these are higher than the statutory medium-term FRBM target of 3%.

 

• The FRBM Act was enacted in 2003 and came into force in 2004.

 

NOTE

 

• Fiscal deficit = total expenditure − total receipts (excluding borrowings). The N.K. Singh panel (2017) suggested a general-government debt-to-GDP ratio of 60% and introduced an escape clause.

question: Which committee was constituted to review and suggest reforms to the FRBM Act?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. N.K. Singh Committee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The committee to review the FRBM Act was set up in 2016 under the chairmanship of N.K. Singh. It recommended a debt-to-GDP ratio as the primary anchor, a fiscal deficit target of 3% of GDP, and the creation of a Fiscal Council.

 

• It also proposed an 'escape clause' allowing deviations from targets during emergencies (war, calamity, sharp downturn).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kelkar Committee (2012): gave a roadmap for fiscal consolidation.

 

• Rangarajan Committee: associated with poverty estimation and balance-of-payments/current account.

 

• Tarapore Committee: dealt with capital account convertibility.

 

NOTE

 

• Committee–topic pairs to revise: N.K. Singh – FRBM review, Bimal Jalan – RBI economic capital, U.K. Sinha – MSMEs, Nachiket Mor – financial inclusion.

question: India is the world's largest producer of which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Milk.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India is the world's largest producer of milk (दूध), accounting for a large share of global output, driven by its huge cattle and buffalo population and the success of the cooperative dairy movement.

 

• The 'White Revolution' (Operation Flood) made India the top milk producer; Verghese Kurien is the 'Father of the White Revolution'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Wheat: wrong – India ranks second (China is the largest).

 

• Rice: wrong – India ranks second (China is the largest).

 

• Sugar: wrong – India is among the top producers but not consistently the single largest of these listed (milk is the clear answer).

 

NOTE

 

• India is also the largest producer of pulses and jute. Revolution hooks: Green (foodgrains), White (milk), Blue (fish), Yellow (oilseeds), Golden (fruits/horticulture).

question: Who was the Union Finance Minister of India when the 1991 economic reforms (Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation) were introduced?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Manmohan Singh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr Manmohan Singh, as Finance Minister under Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao, introduced the landmark 1991 economic reforms (LPG) in response to a severe balance-of-payments crisis.

 

• The reforms marked a shift from a controlled economy to liberalisation, dismantling much of the 'Licence-Permit-Quota Raj'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• P. Chidambaram: later Finance Minister, but not in 1991.

 

• Yashwant Sinha: FM under the NDA (late 1990s–2002), not 1991.

 

• Pranab Mukherjee: FM in the 1980s and again 2009–12, not during the 1991 reforms.

 

NOTE

 

• The 1991 crisis forced India to pledge gold to secure IMF loans. Manmohan Singh later served as Prime Minister (2004–2014).

question: Geetanjali Shree's Hindi novel that won the International Booker Prize in 2022 was ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Tomb of Sand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Tomb of Sand' (original Hindi title 'Ret Samadhi'), written by Geetanjali Shree and translated by Daisy Rockwell, won the International Booker Prize in 2022.

 

• It was the first novel in any Indian language, and the first in Hindi, to win the award. The prize is shared equally by the author and the translator.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Heart Lamp (Banu Mushtaq): won the International Booker in 2025 (Kannada).

 

• Burnt Sugar (Avni Doshi): was shortlisted for the Booker Prize in 2020.

 

• The White Tiger (Aravind Adiga): won the Booker Prize in 2008 (a different award from the International Booker).

 

NOTE

 

• Distinguish the Booker Prize (English-language fiction) from the International Booker Prize (translated fiction). Both awarded annually in the UK.

question: At which Harappan site was the earliest evidence of a ploughed agricultural field discovered?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Kalibangan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kalibangan, in present-day Rajasthan, yielded the earliest evidence of a ploughed field, showing a criss-cross pattern of furrows. It is also famous for its fire altars, suggesting ritual practice.

 

• Kalibangan means 'black bangles' and lies on the banks of the (now dry) Ghaggar river.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lothal (Gujarat): known for its dockyard (earliest known artificial dock).

 

• Dholavira (Gujarat): known for its water-management system and the famous signboard; a UNESCO site.

 

• Banawali (Haryana): known for high-quality barley and both Pre-Harappan and Harappan phases.

 

NOTE

 

• Harappan site–feature pairs: Harappa – granaries; Mohenjodaro – Great Bath; Lothal – dockyard; Kalibangan – ploughed field & fire altars; Dholavira – water reservoirs.

question: In table tennis, how many points must a player score to win a game (except when the score is tied at deuce)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 11.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the rules revised by the ITTF in 2001, a game of table tennis is won by the first player to reach 11 points, provided there is a lead of at least 2 points.

 

• If the score reaches 10–10 (deuce), play continues until one player leads by two points.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• 21: wrong – that was the format before 2001.

 

• 15 / 7: wrong – not table-tennis game scores.

 

• Matches are usually 'best of' an odd number of games (e.g., best of 7).

 

NOTE

 

• Governing body: International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF). Service alternates every 2 points (and every point during deuce).

question: In a standard game of tennis, a player must win at least how many games (with a two-game margin) to win a set?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 6.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In tennis, a set is won by the first player to win 6 games, provided they lead by at least 2 games (e.g., 6–4).

 

• If the score reaches 6–6, a tie-break is usually played to decide the set.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• 4 / 5: wrong – a player needs 6 games (with a 2-game margin) to take a set.

 

• 7: wrong – 7 games win a set only via a tie-break scenario (7–5 or 7–6), not the minimum.

 

• Within a game, scoring runs 15, 30, 40, game (with deuce at 40–40); 'love' means zero.

 

NOTE

 

• A men's Grand Slam match is best of five sets. The four Grand Slams: Australian Open, French Open (Roland Garros), Wimbledon, US Open.

question: In which year did the first electric train run in India, between Bombay's Victoria Terminus and Kurla?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 1925.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's first electric train ran on 3 February 1925 between Victoria Terminus (Mumbai CSMT) and Kurla on the Harbour Line, using 1500 V DC traction.

 

• This followed the first passenger train (Bombay to Thane, ~34 km) which ran in 1853.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• 1853: wrong for this question – that is the year of the first passenger train (steam), Bombay–Thane.

 

• 1900 / 1947: wrong – do not correspond to the first electric train.

 

NOTE

 

• The first Railway Minister of independent India was John Mathai. Key date pairs: 1853 – first passenger train; 1925 – first electric train.

question: Which of the following is an example of an alkaline earth metal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Calcium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Alkaline earth metals belong to Group 2 of the periodic table and include beryllium, magnesium, calcium, strontium, barium and radium. Among the options, Calcium is the alkaline earth metal.

 

• Alkaline earth metals have 2 valence electrons.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sodium: wrong – it is an alkali metal (Group 1).

 

• Aluminium: wrong – it is in Group 13.

 

• Iron: wrong – it is a transition metal.

 

NOTE

 

• Group 1 = alkali metals (Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr); Group 2 = alkaline earth metals (Be, Mg, Ca, Sr, Ba, Ra). Calcium is essential for bones and is present in limestone (CaCO₃).

question: Which of the following is a Tat Vadya (a stringed instrument)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Sarod.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Tat Vadya (तत वाद्य) refers to stringed instruments in the Indian classification of musical instruments. The Sarod is a plucked stringed instrument and thus a Tat Vadya.

 

• The Sarod has a fretless metal fingerboard producing a deep tone; Ustad Amjad Ali Khan is a renowned Sarod maestro.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mridangam: wrong – a percussion instrument (Avanaddha Vadya).

 

• Bansuri: wrong – a wind instrument (Sushir Vadya).

 

• Tabla: wrong – a percussion instrument (Avanaddha Vadya).

 

NOTE

 

• Four classes: Tat (string), Sushir (wind), Avanaddha (membrane/percussion), Ghana (solid/idiophone). Other Tat Vadya: Sitar, Veena, Sarangi, Santoor, Ektara.

question: Which of the following is a Sushir Vadya (a wind instrument)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Shehnai.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sushir Vadya (सुषिर वाद्य) refers to wind instruments in the Indian classification. The Shehnai, played by blowing air through a reed, is a Sushir Vadya.

 

• Ustad Bismillah Khan was the legendary Shehnai maestro (a Bharat Ratna awardee); the Shehnai is traditionally played at weddings and temples.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Veena: wrong – a stringed instrument (Tat Vadya).

 

• Sarod: wrong – a stringed instrument (Tat Vadya).

 

• Tabla: wrong – a percussion instrument (Avanaddha Vadya).

 

NOTE

 

• Other Sushir Vadya: Bansuri (flute), Nadaswaram, Shankh, Harmonium. Ghana Vadya (solid instruments) include Manjira, Ghatam, Jaltarang.
